Asana Reviews & Product Details

Asana is a leading work management platform for human + AI collaboration. Over 170,000 customers like Accenture, Amazon, Anthropic, and Suzuki rely on Asana to align teams and accelerate organizational impact. Whether it’s managing strategic initiatives, cross-functional programs, or company-wide goals, Asana helps organizations bring clarity to complexity—turning plans into action with AI working alongside teams every step of the way. To learn more, visit www.asana.com.

My Tasks is your one-stop-shop for viewing and prioritizing all of the work assigned to you.
Workflow Builder is a tool that makes it easy for teams to visually plan and set up start-to-finish workflows. It helps connect teams and coordinate work across stakeholders.
Home is your personal space in Asana to prioritize your day (or jump back in), see relevant snapshots from across the Asana Work GraphTM, and dive into the work that matters most.
Connect your company goals and the work to support them in one place. You can see progress to keep teams on track. And teams can work smarter to get the right things done.

"Asana Fits Our Team’s Needs with Strong Project Management Features"
5/5
What do you like best about Asana?

Asana's project management features work well enough for our team's needs. I like how tasks can be assigned to specific people and due dates can be set. The calendar view is also pretty solid. We've found it's taken a bit to figure out how to use some of the more advanced features, but overall, it's a good tool. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

Asana's user interface is pretty solid, but I find the default task assignment feature a bit annoying. It took a bit to figure out how to disable it, and I wish there was a more prominent warning about it. It's not a huge deal, but it's something that's bugged me over time. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Asana's helping us solve project management headaches and keep our team on track. We've reduced meeting time by 30% and boosted productivity by 25% since switching from Trello. It's not perfect, but it's pretty solid for our needs. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Intuitive, Easy-to-Navigate Project Management with Asana"
4/5
What do you like best about Asana?

What I like best about Asana is how easy it is to navigate. The interface is intuitive, making it simple to organize tasks, manage projects, and collaborate with team members without a steep learning curve. It has a good variety of features for tracking work and keeping projects on schedule. While I do think it's on the pricier side compared to some alternatives, the overall user experience and ease of use make it a strong project management platform. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

One downside of Asana is its pricing, especially for smaller teams or businesses that need access to premium features. Some useful functionality is locked behind higher-tier plans, which can make the cost add up quickly. I also found that as projects become more complex, managing custom fields, automations, and dependencies can take some time to set up and maintain. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Asana helps us keep projects, tasks, and team communication organized in one place. It makes it easy to assign work, track progress, and stay on top of deadlines, which improves collaboration and reduces the need for constant follow-ups. Having a clear view of project status has also helped us work more efficiently and keep everyone aligned on priorities. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Smooth, Intuitive Project Planning and Task Management in Asana."
4.5/5
What do you like best about Asana?

The process of planning projects and managing tasks in Asana feels smooth and intuitive. Creating projects, creating tasks, setting their dependencies and tracking milestones is easy enough, and having five views available allows to choose the most suitable for the team option. Working with Asana is a joy since all the comments, file attachments, approvals and progress updates are made in one place. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

Asana depends much on the right project management approach. If tasks are not kept up-to-date and the project is not structured, then the visibility drops instantly. There are also some advanced portfolio management, reporting and automation options only available in the highest tiers and there might be difficulties with working in a big workspace. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Asana replaces manual project tracking and communication methods, spreadsheets and various communication tools. As a result of using it, teams receive more ownership and better understanding of the deadlines and priorities of their work, which reduces the amount of confusion and unnecessary communications. Cross-functional collaboration becomes much easier with project discussions, files and task updates being managed in one workspace. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Automates Project Management and Boosts Collaboration"

What do you like best about Asana?

I like the ability to upload documents and files to Asana, which is especially useful for tasks like new onboarding for sponsors where they can upload logos and videos. I also appreciate using forms to start projects and automate the work process by receiving notifications and keeping my team on track. The AI rule creation is improving, allowing me to adjust due dates as needed, assign different individuals to tasks, and move tasks to relevant sections based on the last task completed. These features enhance efficiency and help us stay organized. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

I would love to be able to review a start date and a due date in my tasks or task manager instead of only having the visibility of the due date. I would also love to see more flexibility in the rules and the automation. Today, when I assign another team member a task, they don't see it until the due date. It doesn't pop up on their list, whereas if I could assign a start date and a due date, they would get notified of that instead of it barring out all the dates in between. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

I find Asana helps me maintain consistency in managing events and pipelines without relying on email and Teams, allowing seamless collaboration. Forms shift work to submitters, and AI rules efficiently automate tasks, ensuring progress tracking. Document uploads streamline sponsor onboarding, and aligning tasks with Outlook keeps everything organized. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Intuitive UI, Strong Collaboration, and Handy Slack Integration"
4/5
What do you like best about Asana?

I like the UI/UX aspects of collaboration, custom template, and dependencies features. They help the team stay on the same project and give everyone visibility into the status (or lack thereof) of specific tasks or an overall vertical that we’re working on. Also integration with Slack is helpful because we can pull tasks directly from chats within our DMs or channels. With templates, we can also build in common elements across projects that share the same known tasks, so we don’t miss repeatable steps on specific projects. Being able to analyze common points between tasks ahead of time would make it easier to streamline how we create those templates. And if we already had pre-built dependencies, we could use them as a starting point for suggesting due dates, whether we’re planning forward or working backward from a set deadline. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

I think what is unfortunate, is the lack of ability to custom assign roles. To have all the members we want to have on Asana it's much higher overhead than what's worth spending at this time, however, if there were tiered roles that we could assign and one person (for instance) would have a basic "view" seat at $5/mo but another who's Admin was at a higher $30/mo, with a middle ground of "regular user" being at $15/mo that would allow more of the team to be on the platform, without necessarily having the ability (or need) to utilize the platform to it's full capacity, while also having the company analyze the performance of who actually needs an Admin seat. Also, interchanging those roles would be helpful for onboarding purposes; for instance if a new member joins, and we want to have visibility into a project without them actually being able to mark something as complete - but rather just a backseat watcher, they could have a view only seat so they could track how the status of a task or project goes along the way and when the team is ready they could be moved into a different tier role at a higher price paid seat. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Honestly, prior to utilizing Asana, there was no way of tracking tasks and projects. The KPIs were essentially non visible in the sense of being able to track/prove performance of a team member or overall department. Being able to utilize project tracking status allows us to see how far along each vertical is OR how long a project has to be complete. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Powerful, Intuitive Asana—But Dev-to-UAT Workflows and Pricing Tiers Can Get Tricky"
3.5/5
What do you like best about Asana?

Asana stands out for its intuitive, multi-view interface—offering List, Board, and Timeline formats—alongside robust workflow automation that handles routine status updates, task assignments, and handoffs. Its portfolios and workload tracking provide clear cross-functional visibility, while seamless integrations with tools like Slack, Teams, Figma, and Google Drive keep project context centralized. Coupled with customizable fields and clear dependency tracking, it makes managing complex, multi-team projects effortless and transparent. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

While Asana is exceptional for general task management, tracking complex end-to-end workflows from Dev to UAT to Completion isn't as seamless or structured as dedicated development boards. Its strict single-assignee limit makes shared ownership awkward without adding subtasks, and essential features like advanced automation rules, workload management, and portfolios are locked behind higher-tier plans. Additionally, managing deeply nested subtasks can cause UI clutter, making technical handoffs harder to track at a glance. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

Asana solves the disorganization and manual overhead typical of onboarding and support operations by centralizing multi-step workflows into structured, repeatable processes. Using custom forms and reusable templates, we can seamlessly intake support requests or trigger new client/employee onboarding sequences, automatically assigning ownership and dependencies. This eliminates lost hand-offs between teams, provides real-time visibility into onboarding progress, and ensures customer or internal support inquiries are resolved efficiently without slipping through the cracks. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Asana Keeps Me Organized—Fast, Fair-Priced, and Great Support"
5/5
What do you like best about Asana?

Asana has helped me get organized, hold myself accountable, and meet deadlines that I was missing before because I was losing notes amongst the 15 notepads and legal pads I was writing every single task and thought and reminder in! I LOVE that it can integrate with ChatGPT! That has honestly been the biggest upgrade since I've started using Asana close to a year ago. The price point is very fair, the performance is great - there's never any glitches and it never runs slow, and the support is phenomenal! Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Asana?

Honestly I haven't found any dislikes so far about Asana. I don't think that I use it to its fullest capability because I'm the only one on the team that uses it. It makes for an excellent invoice payment tracker and to do list for me. I color coded the different categories of my day to day tasks (Administrative, HR, Finance, Brain Dump, etc.) and I can look at the calendar view and see very easily what I've got on the docket for that day. It works very well with my ADHD brain! Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Asana solving and how is that benefiting you?

I'm not missing deadlines! And that is benefitting me because my boss is happy and I stay out of trouble lol. Before Asana, I was a hot mess express! Seriously, I can fill a legal pad up from front to back in about three days. With Asana, I can get all of my thoughts out of my head in my Brain Dump project, and then I can go back and sort each task into the appropriate project depending on whether it's HR related, Finance related, or just regular ole Admin related. And no more legal pads stacked up on my desk or shuffling to find notes about x, y, or z. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Seamless Project Management and Team Alignment"

What do you like best about Asana?

I find Asana's user interface to be quite visually appealing and intuitive, which makes it easy to add items or tasks. The ability to toggle between different boards is fairly intuitive as well.
